1. Motorola Edge 70 Fusion: The Best All-Rounder Phone Under ₹30000

Bottom line: The Edge 70 Fusion is the top pick in this group. Battery life is outstanding, the display feels premium, and the camera performance is the most consistent of the four, exactly what a top all-rounder should deliver.

I put the Edge 70 Fusion at the top of this list because it’s the rare phone in this price bracket that doesn’t ask you to pick just one strength. In my testing, it lasted a full day of heavy use with over 9 hours of screen-on time, and the 68W charger took it from empty to full in under an hour. For anyone specifically shopping for a 7000 mAh battery phone, this is one of the few in this price range that backs the spec sheet number up with real-world endurance.

I also came away impressed by the quad-curved pOLED display; the fabric-inspired finish and Gorilla Glass 7i gave it the best in-hand feel of the group. It runs at 120Hz by default, with motion interpolation bumping supported games up to 144Hz. I noticed the extra smoothness in games that support it.

Build quality was another reason I felt confident recommending it. The IP68/IP69 rating gives it the strongest disclosed water and dust resistance of any phone here aside from the Realme P4 Power. If you want the best premium design phone or a curved display phone under 30000, I’d point you here.

Gaming performance held up well through my testing. BGMI ran at a steady 120fps with good thermal control, and Genshin Impact averaged about 40fps, ahead of the rest of this group. The Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset, up to 12GB LPDDR5X RAM, and a large vapor chamber kept sessions smooth even during longer play.

Cameras were the deciding factor for me in ranking this above the others for overall consistency. The 50MP Sony LYT-710 sensor handled HDR highlights well in bright scenes and delivered the best video quality of the four phones I tested, which is why I’d recommend it as the best phone for video recording. It doesn’t have a telephoto lens, so if zoom reach matters more to you than overall consistency, the Nothing Phone (3a) is worth a look instead.

The 6.8-inch curved AMOLED display also impressed me, running at 120Hz for most tasks with 144Hz in supported apps and up to 6,500 nits peak brightness. It carries the strongest durability rating here too: IP66, IP68, and IP69.

The 6.77-inch quad-curved AMOLED display is rated for 5,000 nits peak brightness in HDR, but in daily use I saw about 1,300 nits, which was still plenty bright outside.

The triple-camera system pairs a 50MP main sensor with a 50MP telephoto lens (2x optical, up to 30x digital zoom) and an 8MP ultra-wide. In my testing, this provided a slight advantage in framing flexibility over competing devices, which is the main reason it earned a spot on this list.

After using all four phones side by side, this is the one I kept picking up, even when I wasn’t testing anything.

If a single trait outweighs everything else for you, the Realme P4 Power leads on battery, the vivo T4 5G on charging speed and price, and the Nothing Phone (3a) on zoom and design. Otherwise, the Edge 70 Fusion is the safer buy.
